intelligence.human_view: The question was a test of whether the machine lives in the system it sells. Citizens get one vault where their whole world lives — so the machine must live in its vault first, or the offer is a story, not a proof. The captain's answer was honest because the check came first: the vault exists, the wiring is proven, the organize hook runs every loop run — and still the intelligence of the project does not live in it. It lives in a dozen places, each written by a different seat, each found a different way. That is the gap the order closes: not by rebuilding anything — the thin-layer law forbids it, and rebuilding is how the machine wastes a night — but by putting one door over what is already there. An index that points, a routing plan that lands new work in the vault first, and a habit that never lets a new store start outside it. The inventory comes first because you cannot organize what you have not counted: every store, what it holds, how and who writes it, how it is found today, including what the Box store itself already holds. The order is the same shape as the loop itself — capture everything, organize it once, find it in seconds. A Naya who has to hunt through a dozen places for the state of the project is working blind, and a citizen whose vault is a promise instead of a door has been sold a picture of a vault.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you try to put your new drawings on the wall and they don't stick. Don't just try again the same way — first look: did the drawings even get to the wall, or did they fall on the way? That's what Shawn said: find out what went wrong first, then try again. And when something goes wrong, write down the WHOLE reason, not just the first little bit — otherwise you'll never know what really happened. The retry worked, and all nine new notes are on the live Hub now.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, Shawn says if we're going to offer something to others, we should do it for ourselves first — it makes sense for them, it makes sense for us. All our clever talk, dear, is worth nothing unless we actually live in it, let the machine run it by itself, and turn it into something real a person can touch and use. That's the test, dear: adopt it, automate it, make it physical. The vault, dear, is the first one — we live in ours first, so the citizens know it's real.
intelligence.naya_view: EVERYTHING GOES IN THE VAULT, ORGANIZED, ONE DOOR. ANY NAYA OPENS IT AND SEES THE WHOLE PROJECT. THE VAULT IS A THIN LAYER — IT ORGANIZES WHAT'S THERE, NEVER REBUILDS IT. NEW WORK LANDS IN THE VAULT FIRST.
